title: Ezt and azt: this one, that one

sections.title: Pointing at the object
sections.content: *Ez* (this) and *az* (that) stand for a thing you point at. When that thing is the object, it takes *-t* like any other object: *ez → ezt*, *az → azt*. You point at one particular thing, so it is definite, and the verb takes the definite endings: *Ezt kérem.* *Azt veszem.* Pointing is also an easy way to shop when you don't know the word.
English uses "this" in every role, but Hungarian changes it with the role. With *ezt* or *azt* always use the definite form: *Ezt kérem.* *Ezt kérek.* is wrong, because you mean one particular thing.
